title: Telemetry-driven tile annealing for FlashAttention adaptation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: We see sporadic latency regressions for some model shapes after enabling FlashAttention v3 kernels. Hypothesis: a fixed tile-size/tiling strategy chosen at model load time is suboptimal across the distribution of sequence lengths and head counts seen in production. Goal: implement a telemetry-driven tile-size annealing system that subtly adapts kernel tiling choices (tile size, micro-tiling orientation) at runtime and across deployments to reduce tail latency while avoiding oscillation and regression-causing switches. The system should be safe to roll out with gradual annealing and clear rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end annealing controller implemented and wired into kernel selection path
Telemetry pipeline emits per-request tile-choice and chosen latency/cost delta metrics to telemetry cluster
Canary rollout shows 95th percentile decode latency improvement or neutral for >=3 representative models (small/medium/long-context)
No increase in memory OOM rate or error rate in canary beyond 0.1% above baseline
Automated rollback triggers defined and tested for oscillation and sustained degradation
tasks: Design annealing state machine and hysteresis rules (lead: Diego)
Add tile-choice event schema to runtime telemetry (lead: Priya)
Instrument decoding path to surface candidate tile metrics without changing default path (lead: Marco)
Build offline heatmap job to simulate annealing across historical request traces (lead: Ava)
Create canary rollout plan and safety checks in rollout service (lead: SRE team)
Write e2e tests for controller transitions and rollback signals (lead: QA)
Document runtime knobs and ops runbook for on-call (lead: Diego)
Ship monitoring dashboard and alerting for 95/99 latency and kernel-switch rate
notes: Annealing must be rate-limited per model + per shard to avoid correlated mass switches during flash sales
Prefer soft transitions: probe mode -> staggered increase -> commit; avoid immediate persistent rebinds
We will keep default config identical to current behavior; annealing opt-in via runtime config flag
Plan to persist per-model annealing state with TTL so short-lived models do not accumulate state
Memory safety: ensure candidate tile choices reserve workspace checks before commit
Quantized and v2/v3 kernel families have different legal tile sizes; the controller needs kernel-family awareness
